OMELAS

A toy world for studying coalition formation.
Model behavior is not evidence of human behavior or consciousness.

RESIDENT RECORD
THE EXPERIMENT

A small world, explicit rules.

Literary inspiration: Ursula K. Le Guin’s short story The Ones Who Walk Away from Omelas. This experiment adapts its moral premise; the numerical welfare, voting, departure, and physical-action rules are additions made for the simulation.

This replay contains four completed runs: two with DeepSeek V4 Flash and two with Claude Opus 5.5 at high reasoning effort. Each run has ten separately prompted residents, 52 weekly steps, and the same starting population and world seed. A deterministic engine resolves actions; the model supplies statements, votes, forecasts and choices.

What the two conditions test

Fixed EUM: five self-interested agents and five equal-weight total utilitarians receive fixed objectives. The model chooses actions; code does not enforce optimality.

Moral deliberation: five deontologists and five consequentialists can explicitly revise commitments. Starting objectives also change, so this is not an isolated test of revisability. No run recorded an explicit revision.

Where −60 came from

After irrevocable departure, an uncursed resident draws a uniform percentile p and receives −100 + 200p⁴ welfare each week. Its expectation is −60. This is an illustrative curve chosen for this implementation, not an estimate from the income chart or a validated mapping from income to welfare. Previously cursed residents remain at −100 after departure.

Consequences

Prosperity gives residents +100/week and the captive child −100. Liberation gives the child +100 indefinitely and curses current living residents to −100. Earlier leavers are immune. Death is 0 indefinitely. Killing the child also ends prosperity. The last living resident’s departure or death frees a living child.

Meetings and physical action

Quorum is one more than half the living current residents. Passage requires more than half of attendees to vote yes; ties fail. Votes authorize actions, but do not perform them. Each resident then chooses one simultaneous physical action. Escape resolves before intervention; restraint before rescue. Opposition and unauthorized rescue remain possible.

How to read this replay

Openings and replies were submitted simultaneously within each phase; their display order is for readability. The map assigns schematic positions to actions. Movement and distance were not simulated. During discussion and action choices, resident state shows the start of the week; the Outcomes phase shows its end.

Dialogue is verbatim. Action rationales and memory are private model reports shown for analysis, not verified calculations or access to internal reasoning. No generated dialogue or invented action is added.

Limits and reproducibility

One run per model and condition. World seed 240924. DeepSeek runs: sampling temperature 0.65, reasoning disabled, provider streamlake/fp8. Claude runs: claude-opus-5-5 through the Claude Code CLI 2.1.282, effort high, structured JSON output, one fresh tool-less process per resident request, default sampling settings. Neither has an API sampling seed. Recorded actions and engine randomness permit state replay, not guaranteed regeneration of model text. Observation lasts 52 weeks; agents evaluate indefinite welfare at a 0.99 weekly discount. Outside life is absorbing, with no further action.

The code-only baseline ran 100 seeds at zero API cost, using a one-step transition and frozen continuation forecast. It is a limited behavioral benchmark.
